subject: Alignment: temporary log custody & backup purge sequencing (BrightPath)
messages:
From: Dana Liu <dana.liu@brightpathlabs.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>
Cc: BrightPath Security Team <security@brightpathlabs.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: short-term hold + backup purge dates for upcoming BrightPath audit

Hi Nikhil,

We're ramping for a compliance review the week of Aug 30 and need to line up retention and purge timelines for logs and backups that contain customer identifiers. Two asks to start:

1) Can Redwood commit to a short-term 45-day retention hold for the set of logs tied to our account (all kv-log partitions for region us-west)? We understand this is temporary and would like an ops-and-legal-approved runbook.

2) Second, please confirm the next backup purge date after Aug 30 and what the restore window would be if we need to pull artifacts for the audit.

I've attached our audit timeline and a DPA draft with our proposed addendum language. If this needs approval from your legal, please route accordingly — timelines are tight.

Thanks,
Dana
Dana Liu
Security Program Manager
BrightPath Labs
attachments: BrightPath_audit_timeline.xlsx; BrightPath_DPA_v3_redlines.pdf
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>
To: Dana Liu <dana.liu@brightpathlabs.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Jul 2026 12:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: short-term hold + backup purge dates for upcoming BrightPath audit

Hi Dana — thanks for the heads-up and the doc. Short answer: we can support a temporary short-term hold, but we need to coordinate ops, legal, and our subprocessor attestations. Proposed approach below (ops + legal signoff required):

- Temporary hold window: 45 days from Aug 30 (so hold until Oct 14). This will be a metadata-level custody flag preventing normal purge jobs from targeting BrightPath partitions.
- Purge schedule: our next automated backup prune currently scheduled Sept 10; we propose to skip BrightPath partitions during that run and resume normal prune on Oct 15.
- Restore window: we can stage a 7-day restore environment inside a secure VPC for audit extraction. Leads must request restores at least 5 business days before the extraction window.
- Subprocessor attestations: ops will need signed confirmation from any downstream storage subprocessor that they will honor the temporary hold. Legal will need to sign a DPA addendum or equivalent.

Marissa, can you confirm operations can implement the metadata hold and provide the runbook excerpt?

Dana, copying Kimberly from Legal to coordinate the DPA addendum language.

Regards,
Nikhil Sharma
Director, Customer Security
Redwood Inference

On Wed, Jul 28, 2026 at 09:12 AM Dana Liu <dana.liu@brightpathlabs.com> wrote:
> We're ramping for a compliance review the week of Aug 30...
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Dana Liu <dana.liu@brightpathlabs.com>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Jul 2026 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: short-term hold + backup purge dates for upcoming BrightPath audit

Hi Dana / Nikhil — legal here. We can accept a scoped DPA addendum for a temporary retention carveout; a few guardrails to note:

1) Scope & duration: addendum must explicitly name the affected data types (kv-log partitions tied to account id BP-2026-014) and cap the hold at 45 days, with an optional single 14-day extension only with mutual written approval.
2) Subprocessor flow-down: Redwood requires documented attestation from each subprocessor that stores backups or logs (S3/managed archive and third-party snapshot services). We have an internal attestation template; Marissa, please use the template and collect signatures.
3) Cross-border: If any of the backup shards reside in EU zones, the addendum must reference the SCCs or our EU transfer mechanism; we can do a targeted carveout but will need explicit subprocessor certification for cross-border transfer during the hold.
4) Audit access: the addendum should restrict extract access to named BrightPath auditors and define the secure transfer mechanism (SFTP to a pre-approved IP or access through a read-only helper VM).

I will prepare redline suggestions on the DPA draft and upload to DocuSign for signature. Anticipating we need a 48-hour legal turnaround to meet your timeline.

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Sr. Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference
attachments: temp-retain-runbook.md
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Dana Liu <dana.liu@brightpathlabs.com>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Jul 2026 15:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: short-term hold + backup purge dates for upcoming BrightPath audit

Hi Dana — operations confirmation and schedule below.

- Implementation: Ops will set a custody flag on all BrightPath kv-log partitions in us-west by EOD Aug 29. That flag prevents the Sept 10 prune job from deleting any objects with the BrightPath tag.
- Restore capability: We'll provision a timeboxed restore environment (read-only) for the dates Aug 30 - Sep 06; requests for specific extractions must arrive by Aug 23.
- Subprocessor attestations: I'll initiate the attestation requests today using Kim's template. Expect first-round responses within 5 business days.
- Contingencies: If a subprocessor refuses, we will notify BrightPath and propose either (a) alternate evidence plan (logs + hash attestations) or (b) a short escrow snapshot paired with on-site review.

Thanks,
